title: Emperor Maximilian Grotto Zirl
name: Emperor Maximilian Grotto Zirl
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiser-Maximilian-Grotte in the Martinswand near Zirl: legendary rock cave high above the Inntal with a large crucifix and panoramic views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The steeped-in-history Kaiser-Maximilian-Grotte (often referred to simply as Maximiliangrotte) is nestled in the dizzyingly steep rock face of the world-famous Martinswand within the municipality of Zirl in the Inntal (district of Innsbruck-Land). Located around ten kilometers west of Tyrol's capital Innsbruck, this striking rock cave sits at an altitude of approximately 850 meters above sea level, about 250 meters vertically above the floor of the Inntal. This spectacular site combines a dramatic alpine rock backdrop with one of Tyrol's most famous imperial legends.

Historical Legend & Crucifix

The fame of the cave dates back to a dramatic event in the year 1499: according to legend, the hunting-enthusiast Habsburg Emperor Maximilian I. ventured into the rugged precipices of the Martinswand while hunting chamois, became hopelessly stranded in the brittle limestone cliffs, and could move neither forward nor backward. After enduring days of mortal terror, an angel in the guise of a simple peasant lad is said to have appeared to him and guided him safely out of the perilous cliff face. In eternal gratitude for his miraculous rescue, Kaiser Maximilian commissioned the enlargement of the spacious natural cave and adorned it with a monumental, widely visible wooden crucifix alongside statues of the Virgin Mary and the Apostle John. To this day, the cave remains an important cultural monument and a popular destination for sure-footed hikers and mountaineers.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaiser-Maximilian-Grotte is open and freely accessible free of charge during the snow-free season from May to October (closed in winter due to snow and rockfall hazard). Access is via a secured yet occasionally exposed mountain trail that requires surefootedness and a head for heights (walking time from the valley approx. 45 minutes). Getting there by car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Zirl Ost) or the B171 to the Martinswand; parking is available at the Martinswand climbers' car park along the federal highway. By public transport: Take the ÖBB/S-Bahn to Hochzirl or Zirl station, from where a hiking trail leads to the start of the cave path.

Tips

Sturdy mountain boots with good tread are strictly required for the ascent to the cave; the trail is not suitable for small children or inexperienced walkers. Climbing enthusiasts will discover world-renowned sport climbing crags and the popular Kaiser-Max-Klettersteig via ferrata on the surrounding cliffs of the Martinswand. From the cave platform, you can enjoy a breathtaking plunging view down onto the Inn river and across to the Stubaier Alpen.
